paper_title: A New Electron Acceptor with meta-Alkoxyphenyl Side Chain for Fullerene-Free Polymer Solar Cells with 9.3% Efficiency
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Science - 2017 - Zhang - A New Electron Acceptor with meta‐Alkoxyphenyl Side Chain for Fullerene‐Free Polymer/auto/Advanced Science - 2017 - Zhang - A New Electron Acceptor with meta‐Alkoxyphenyl Side Chain for Fullerene‐Free Polymer.md

knowledge_points.content: The small molecule acceptor m-ITIC-OR is synthesized using an indacenodithieno[3,2-b]thiophene (IDTT) core, four meta-alkoxyphenyl side chains, and 2-(3-oxo-2,3-dihydroinden-1-ylidene)malononitrile (IC) end groups.
knowledge_points.evidence: Based on the above considerations, we first synthesized a new acceptor, namely, m-ITIC-OR, based on IDTT as a core with four meta-alkoxyphenyl as side chains as well as IC as an end group.

knowledge_points.content: Additive-free polymer solar cells based on the HFQx-T:m-ITIC-OR blend achieved a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 9.3% after thermal annealing at 150 °C for 5 minutes.
knowledge_points.evidence: Through a simple TA treatment at 150 °C for 5 min, an impressive PCE of 9.3% is obtained. This efficiency is among one of the highest PCEs for additive free PSCs.

knowledge_points.content: Compared to alkylphenyl side chains, alkoxyphenyl groups in nonfullerene acceptors are easier to synthesize via etherification, lower in cost, and exhibit higher coplanarity.
knowledge_points.evidence: alkoxyphenyl group seemed more easily synthesized via simple etherification, much lower cost, and more coplanar compared to its alkyl counterpart.

knowledge_points.content: The m-ITIC-OR acceptor possesses a HOMO energy level of -5.65 eV and a LUMO energy level of -3.97 eV, providing a LUMO offset of 0.47 eV and a HOMO offset of 0.20 eV when paired with the HFQx-T donor.
knowledge_points.evidence: the HOMO energy levels (EHOMO) and LUMO energy levels (ELUMO) of m-ITIC-OR were estimated to be -5.65 and -3.97 eV... The EHOMO and ELUMO of HFQx-T donor were also measured to be -5.45 and -3.50 eV... Notably, the LUMO energy offset (ΔELUMO) between HFQx-T and m-ITIC-OR is 0.47 eV... HOMO energy offset (ΔEHOMO) is only 0.20 eV.

knowledge_points.content: Thermal annealing treatment at 150 °C significantly improves the short-circuit current (Jsc) from 13.48 to 16.15 mA cm⁻² and the fill factor (FF) from 0.50 to 0.64 in HFQx-T:m-ITIC-OR devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: The PSCs based on HFQx-T:m-ITIC-OR blend films showed a PCE of 6.36% with a Voc of 0.95 V, a Jsc of 13.48 mA cm−2, and a FF of 0.50. With 1:1 D/A weight ratio, the PCE was further improved to 9.3% with a Voc of 0.90 V, a higher Jsc of 16.15 mA cm−2, and a FF of 0.64 by TA treatment at 150 °C for 5 min.

knowledge_points.content: The m-ITIC-OR thin film exhibits a maximum absorption coefficient of 7.8 × 10⁴ cm⁻¹ at an absorption maximum (λmax) of 690 nm and an optical bandgap of 1.65 eV.
knowledge_points.evidence: The absorption maximum (λmax) of m-ITIC-OR film was at 690 nm with a maximum absorption coefficient of 7.8 × 104 cm−1. m-ITIC-OR had absorption edge (λedge) of 750 nm and the corresponding optical bandgap (Egopt = 1240/λedge) was 1.65 eV.

knowledge_points.content: The optimized device architecture for the HFQx-T:m-ITIC-OR solar cell is a conventional structure consisting of ITO/PEDOT:PSS/active layer/PDINO/Al.
knowledge_points.evidence: we fabricated PSCs with conventional structure of indium tin oxide (ITO)/poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate)(PEDOT:PSS)/active layer/PDI functionalized with amino N-oxide (PDINO)/Al.

knowledge_points.content: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that thermal annealing transforms the HFQx-T:m-ITIC-OR blend from an amorphous state into a nanoscale interpenetrating network with small crystalline grains.
knowledge_points.evidence: without TA, little large phase separation and amorphous regions in the HFQx-T:m-ITIC-OR blend films could be observed. In contrast, very homogeneous and interpenetrating networks with small crystalline grains uniformly covering the entire scan area can be seen only after TA.
